Is it true that\n    17→  ω₁² → (ω₁·ω, G)²?\n    18→\n    19→Tags: graph theory, ramsey theory, set theory\n    20→-/\n    21→\n    22→/-- The type of ordinals strictly less than α. -/\n    23→abbrev OrdinalSet (α : Ordinal) := {a : Ordinal // a < α}\n    24→\n    25→/-- A graph G contains a complete bipartite subgraph K_{κ,κ} if there exist\n    26→    disjoint vertex sets A and B, each of cardinality at least κ,\n    27→    such that every vertex in A is adjacent to every vertex in B. -/\n    28→def SimpleGraph.ContainsBiclique {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (κ : Cardinal) : Prop :=\n    29→  ∃ (A B : Set V), Disjoint A B ∧ #A ≥ κ ∧ #B ≥ κ ∧\n    30→    ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ B, G.Adj a b\n    31→\n    32→/-- The ordinal-graph partition relation α → (β, G)²:\n    33→    Every 2-coloring of ordered pairs from OrdinalSet α yields either:\n    34→    - an order-embedded copy of β whose pairs are all colored 0, or\n    35→    - a copy of G in the color-1 graph (an injective map preserving edges).\n    36→\n    37→    Here a \"copy of β\" is given by an order embedding e : OrdinalSet β ↪o OrdinalSet α,\n    38→    and monochromaticity means f (e i) (e j) = 0 for all i < j. A \"copy of G\"\n    39→    is an injective map g : V → OrdinalSet α such that every edge of G maps to\n    40→    a pair colored 1. -/\n    41→def OrdGraphPartition (α β : Ordinal) {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=\n    42→  ∀ (f : OrdinalSet α → OrdinalSet α → Fin 2),\n    43→    (∃ e : OrdinalSet β ↪o OrdinalSet α,\n    44→      ∀ i j : OrdinalSet β, i < j → f (e i) (e j) = 0) ∨\n    45→    (∃ g : V → OrdinalSet α, Function.Injective g ∧\n    46→      ∀ u v : V, G.Adj u v → g u < g v → f (g u) (g v) = 1)\n    47→\n    48→/--\n    49→Erdős Problem #597 [Er87] [Va99, 7.84]:\n    50→\n    51→If G is a graph on at most ℵ₁ vertices containing no K₄ and no K_{ℵ₀,ℵ₀},\n    52→then ω₁² → (ω₁·ω, G)².\n    53→\n    54→Erdős and Hajnal proved that ω₁² → (ω₁·ω, 3)². Erdős originally asked this\n    55→with just the assumption that G is K₄-free, but Baumgartner proved that\n    56→ω₁² ↛ (ω₁·ω, K_{ℵ₀,ℵ₀})².\n    57→-/\n    58→theorem erdos_problem_597 {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)\n    59→    (hcard : #V ≤ aleph 1)\n    60→    (hK4 : G.CliqueFree 4)\n    61→    (hbip : ¬G.ContainsBiclique (aleph 0)) :\n    62→    OrdGraphPartition\n    63→      ((aleph 1).ord ^ 2)\n    64→      ((aleph 1).ord * (aleph 0).ord)\n    65→      G :=\n    66→  sorry\n    67→\n    68→end\n    69→"}]},"uuid":"6ff68722-370c-4dad-8786-9bf2f6708b63","timestamp":"2026-02-23T02:26:23.765Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/ryan/erdos/conjectures/597.lean","content":"import Mathlib.SetTheory.Ordinal.Basic\nimport Mathlib.SetTheory.Ordinal.Arithmetic\nimport Mathlib.SetTheory.Cardinal.Aleph\nimport Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic\nimport Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique\nimport Mathlib.Order.Hom.Basic\n\nopen Cardinal SimpleGraph\n\nnoncomputable section\n\n/-!\n# Erdős Problem #597\n\nLet G be a graph on at most ℵ₁ vertices which contains no K₄ and no K_{ℵ₀,ℵ₀}\n(the complete bipartite graph with ℵ₀ vertices in each class). Is it true that\n  ω₁² → (ω₁·ω, G)²?\n\nTags: graph theory, ramsey theory, set theory\n-/\n\n/-- The type of ordinals strictly less than α. -/\nabbrev OrdinalSet (α : Ordinal) := {a : Ordinal // a < α}\n\n/-- A graph G contains a complete bipartite subgraph K_{κ,κ} if there exist\n    disjoint vertex sets A and B, each of cardinality at least κ,\n    such that every vertex in A is adjacent to every vertex in B. -/\ndef SimpleGraph.ContainsBiclique {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (κ : Cardinal) : Prop :=\n  ∃ (A B : Set V), Disjoint A B ∧ #A ≥ κ ∧ #B ≥ κ ∧\n    ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ B, G.Adj a b\n\n/-- The ordinal-graph partition relation α → (β, G)²:\n    Every 2-coloring of ordered pairs from OrdinalSet α yields either:\n    - an order-embedded copy of β whose pairs are all colored 0, or\n    - a copy of G in the color-1 graph (an injective map preserving edges).\n\n    Here a \"copy of β\" is given by an order embedding e : OrdinalSet β ↪o OrdinalSet α,\n    and monochromaticity means f (e i) (e j) = 0 for all i < j. A \"copy of G\"\n    is an injective map g : V → OrdinalSet α such that every edge of G maps to\n    a pair colored 1. -/\ndef OrdGraphPartition (α β : Ordinal) {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=\n  ∀ (f : OrdinalSet α → OrdinalSet α → Fin 2),\n    (∃ e : OrdinalSet β ↪o OrdinalSet α,\n      ∀ i j : OrdinalSet β, i < j → f (e i) (e j) = 0) ∨\n    (∃ g : V → OrdinalSet α, Function.Injective g ∧\n      ∀ u v : V, G.Adj u v → g u < g v → f (g u) (g v) = 1)\n\n/--\nErdős Problem #597 [Er87] [Va99, 7.84]:\n\nIf G is a graph on at most ℵ₁ vertices containing no K₄ and no K_{ℵ₀,ℵ₀},\nthen ω₁² → (ω₁·ω, G)².\n\nErdős and Hajnal proved that ω₁² → (ω₁·ω, 3)². Erdős originally asked this\nwith just the assumption that G is K₄-free, but Baumgartner proved that\nω₁² ↛ (ω₁·ω, K_{ℵ₀,ℵ₀})².\n-/\ntheorem erdos_problem_597 {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)\n    (hcard : #V ≤ aleph 1)\n    (hK4 : G.CliqueFree 4)\n    (hbip : ¬G.ContainsBiclique (aleph 0)) :\n    OrdGraphPartition\n      ((aleph 1).ord ^ 2)\n      ((aleph 1).ord * (aleph 0).ord)\n      G :=\n  sorry\n\nend\n","numLines":69,"startLine":1,"totalLines":69}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"188431ff-5f4a-457f-b954-2b0eb813733b"}

What is the maximum number of edges that a graph on n vertices can\n    16→contain if it does not have a k-regular subgraph? Is it ≪ n^{1+o(1)}?\n    17→\n    18→Asked by Erdős and Sauer. Resolved by Janzer and Sudakov [JaSu23], who proved\n    19→that there exists some C = C(k) > 0 such that any graph on n vertices with at\n    20→least C·n·log(log(n)) edges contains a k-regular subgraph.\n    21→\n    22→A construction due to Pyber, Rödl, and Szemerédi [PRS95] shows that this\n    23→bound is best possible up to the value of the constant C(k).\n    24→-/\n    25→\n    26→/-- G contains a k-regular subgraph: there exists a nonempty finite graph H that\n    27→    is k-regular (every vertex has degree exactly k) and admits an injective\n    28→    graph homomorphism into G. -/\n    29→def containsKRegularSubgraph182 {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=\n    30→  ∃ (U : Type) (fU : Fintype U) (_ : Nonempty U) (H : SimpleGraph U) (dH : DecidableRel H.Adj),\n    31→    haveI := fU; haveI := dH;\n    32→    (∀ v : U, H.degree v = k) ∧\n    33→    ∃ f : U → V, Function.Injective f ∧ ∀ u v : U, H.Adj u v → G.Adj (f u) (f v)\n    34→\n    35→/--\n    36→Erdős Problem #182 (Erdős-Sauer conjecture) [Er75, Er81]:\n    37→\n    38→For every k ≥ 3, there exists a constant C > 0 such that for all sufficiently\n    39→large n, every simple graph on n vertices with at least C · n · log(log(n))\n    40→edges contains a k-regular subgraph.\n    41→\n    42→Proved by Janzer and Sudakov [JaSu23].\n    43→-/\n    44→theorem erdos_problem_182 :\n    45→    ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k →\n    46→    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ n₀ : ℕ,\n    47→    ∀ (n : ℕ), n₀ ≤ n →\n    48→    ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (dG : DecidableRel G.Adj),\n    49→      haveI := dG;\n    50→      (G.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) ≥ C * (n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)) →\n    51→      containsKRegularSubgraph182 G k :=\n    52→  sorry\n    53→\n    54→end\n    55→"}]},"uuid":"61a5b7e5-45b1-44d8-b649-c1afcd49a978","timestamp":"2026-02-20T22:44:13.197Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/ryan/erdos/conjectures/182.lean","content":"import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic\nimport Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite\nimport Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic\nimport Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Card\nimport Mathlib.Data.Finset.Card\nimport Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Basic\n\nopen SimpleGraph\n\nnoncomputable section\n\n/-!\n# Erdős Problem #182\n\nLet k ≥ 3. What is the maximum number of edges that a graph on n vertices can\ncontain if it does not have a k-regular subgraph? Is it ≪ n^{1+o(1)}?\n\nAsked by Erdős and Sauer. Resolved by Janzer and Sudakov [JaSu23], who proved\nthat there exists some C = C(k) > 0 such that any graph on n vertices with at\nleast C·n·log(log(n)) edges contains a k-regular subgraph.\n\nA construction due to Pyber, Rödl, and Szemerédi [PRS95] shows that this\nbound is best possible up to the value of the constant C(k).\n-/\n\n/-- G contains a k-regular subgraph: there exists a nonempty finite graph H that\n    is k-regular (every vertex has degree exactly k) and admits an injective\n    graph homomorphism into G. -/\ndef containsKRegularSubgraph182 {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=\n  ∃ (U : Type) (fU : Fintype U) (_ : Nonempty U) (H : SimpleGraph U) (dH : DecidableRel H.Adj),\n    haveI := fU; haveI := dH;\n    (∀ v : U, H.degree v = k) ∧\n    ∃ f : U → V, Function.Injective f ∧ ∀ u v : U, H.Adj u v → G.Adj (f u) (f v)\n\n/--\nErdős Problem #182 (Erdős-Sauer conjecture) [Er75, Er81]:\n\nFor every k ≥ 3, there exists a constant C > 0 such that for all sufficiently\nlarge n, every simple graph on n vertices with at least C · n · log(log(n))\nedges contains a k-regular subgraph.\n\nProved by Janzer and Sudakov [JaSu23].\n-/\ntheorem erdos_problem_182 :\n    ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k →\n    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ n₀ : ℕ,\n    ∀ (n : ℕ), n₀ ≤ n →\n    ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (dG : DecidableRel G.Adj),\n      haveI := dG;\n      (G.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) ≥ C * (n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)) →\n      containsKRegularSubgraph182 G k :=\n  sorry\n\nend\n","numLines":55,"startLine":1,"totalLines":55}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"36f518b8-8884-412d-ba49-6d11a4070e22"}

Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic\nimport Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Connectivity.Connected\nimport Mathlib.Data.Finset.Basic\nimport Mathlib.Data.Set.Card\nimport Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic\nimport Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real\nimport Mathlib.Order.Filter.AtTopBot.Basic\n\nopen SimpleGraph Real Filter\n\nnoncomputable section\n\n/-!\n# Erdős Problem #150\n\nA minimal cut of a graph is a minimal set of vertices whose removal disconnects\nthe graph. Let c(n) be the maximum number of minimal cuts a graph on n vertices\ncan have. Does c(n)^(1/n) → α for some α < 2?\n\nAsked by Erdős and Nešetřil. Seymour observed that c(3m+2) ≥ 3^m via m\nindependent paths of length 4 joining two vertices.\n\nProved by Bradač [Br24]: the limit α = lim c(n)^(1/n) exists and\nα ≤ 2^H(1/3) = 1.8899... < 2, where H(·) is the binary entropy function.\nThis confirms the conjecture. Bradač conjectures the true value is α = 3^(1/3).\n-/\n\n/-- A set S of vertices is a vertex separator of G if the subgraph induced by\n    the complement V \\ S is not connected. -/\ndef IsVertexSeparator {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=\n  ¬(G.induce ((S : Set (Fin n))ᶜ)).Connected\n\n/-- S is a minimal vertex cut of G if S is a vertex separator and no proper\n    subset of S is also a vertex separator. -/\ndef IsMinimalVertexCut {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=\n  IsVertexSeparator G S ∧\n  ∀ T : Finset (Fin n), T ⊂ S → ¬IsVertexSeparator G T\n\n/-- The number of minimal vertex cuts of G. -/\nnoncomputable def numMinimalVertexCuts {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : ℕ :=\n  Set.ncard { S : Finset (Fin n) | IsMinimalVertexCut G S }\n\n/-- c(n) is the maximum number of minimal vertex cuts over all connected simple\n    graphs on n vertices. -/\nnoncomputable def c (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=\n  sSup { k : ℕ | ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.Connected ∧\n    numMinimalVertexCuts G = k }\n\n/--\nErdős Problem #150 [Er88] (asked by Erdős and Nešetřil):\nLet c(n) be the maximum number of minimal vertex cuts in a graph on n vertices.\nDoes c(n)^(1/n) → α for some α < 2?\n\nProved by Bradač [Br24]: the limit α = lim c(n)^(1/n) exists and\nα ≤ 2^H(1/3) = 1.8899... < 2, where H(·) is the binary entropy function.\nSeymour's construction gives c(3m+2) ≥ 3^m, so α ≥ 3^(1/3) ≈ 1.442.\nBradač conjectures that the true value is α = 3^(1/3).\n-/\ntheorem erdos_problem_150 :\n    ∃ α : ℝ, α < 2 ∧\n      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (c n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)))\n        atTop (nhds α) :=\n  sorry\n\nend\n","numLines":66,"startLine":1,"totalLines":66}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"e5509360-8ece-49b3-a518-017aa5323471"}

The best known upper bound is ≤ 0.5611666 C(n, 3)\n    55→due to Razborov [Ra10].\n    56→-/\n    57→theorem erdos_problem_500 :\n    58→    Tendsto\n    59→      (fun n : ℕ => (ex3K43 n : ℝ) / (Nat.choose n 3 : ℝ))\n    60→      atTop (nhds (5 / 9 : ℝ)) :=\n    61→  sorry\n    62→\n    63→end\n    64→"}]},"uuid":"6a86b9c0-33d5-4f2d-bf4b-7bcc5fe0e25a","timestamp":"2026-02-21T09:08:08.053Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/ryan/erdos/conjectures/500.lean","content":"import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Basic\nimport Mathlib.Data.Finset.Powerset\nimport Mathlib.Data.Nat.Choose.Basic\nimport Mathlib.Data.Nat.Lattice\nimport Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic\nimport Mathlib.Order.Filter.AtTopBot.Basic\nimport Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Basic\n\nopen Finset Filter\n\nnoncomputable section\n\n/-!\n# Erdős Problem #500\n\nWhat is ex₃(n, K₄³)? That is, the largest number of 3-edges which can be placed\non n vertices so that there exists no K₄³, a set of 4 vertices which is covered\nby all 4 possible 3-edges.\n\nA problem of Turán. Turán observed that dividing the vertices into three equal\nparts X₁, X₂, X₃, and taking the edges to be those triples that either have\nexactly one vertex in each part or two vertices in Xᵢ and one vertex in Xᵢ₊₁\n(where X₄ = X₁) shows that\n\n  ex₃(n, K₄³) ≥ (5/9 + o(1)) C(n, 3).\n\nThis is probably the truth. The current best upper bound is\n\n  ex₃(n, K₄³) ≤ 0.5611666 C(n, 3),\n\ndue to Razborov [Ra10].\n-/\n\n/-- A 3-uniform hypergraph on `Fin n` is K₄³-free if every edge has exactly 3\n    vertices and no 4 vertices span all 4 possible 3-element subsets. -/\ndef IsK43Free {n : ℕ} (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) : Prop :=\n  (∀ e ∈ H, e.card = 3) ∧\n  ∀ S : Finset (Fin n), S.card = 4 → ¬(S.powersetCard 3 ⊆ H)\n\n/-- The 3-uniform Turán number ex₃(n, K₄³): the maximum number of 3-element subsets\n    of an n-element set such that no 4 vertices span all 4 triples. -/\nnoncomputable def ex3K43 (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=\n  sSup {m : ℕ | ∃ H : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), IsK43Free H ∧ H.card = m}\n\n/--\nErdős Conjecture (Problem #500) — Turán's Hypergraph Conjecture [Er61][Er71][Er74c][Er81]:\n\nThe 3-uniform Turán density for K₄³ is exactly 5/9. Equivalently,\n\n  ex₃(n, K₄³) / C(n, 3) → 5/9 as n → ∞.\n\nTurán conjectured that the lower bound construction (partition into 3 equal parts,\ntake triples with one vertex in each part or two in Xᵢ and one in Xᵢ₊₁) is\noptimal. This remains open. The best known upper bound is ≤ 0.5611666 C(n, 3)\ndue to Razborov [Ra10].\n-/\ntheorem erdos_problem_500 :\n    Tendsto\n      (fun n : ℕ => (ex3K43 n : ℝ) / (Nat.choose n 3 : ℝ))\n      atTop (nhds (5 / 9 : ℝ)) :=\n  sorry\n\nend\n","numLines":64,"startLine":1,"totalLines":64}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"4667655b-4c15-46ef-b798-ed7f5d3c26b2"}
